input.question: How come drinking salt water dehydrates you, but having a salt/water mix in a saline IV hydrates you? Why don’t they just use regular water?
input.ground_truth: It depends on how salty the water is. The saline in IV bags has the same salinity as human blood. Drinking beverages with the proper amount of electrolytes will not dehydrate you(Gatorade for example). Using pure water in IV bags would dilute your blood and cause complications. Drinking sea water, which has way higher salinity than human blood dehydrates you because the increase in sodium causes more water to be excreted as urine.

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: How come drinking salt water dehydrates you, but having a salt/water mix in a saline IV hydrates you? Why don’t they just use regular water?

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine your body is like a little plant that needs just the right kind of water to stay healthy.

When you **drink salt water from the ocean**, it’s like trying to water your plant with really, really salty water. The salt in that water is so much that it pulls water out of your body instead of putting it in! So, you actually lose more water than you get, and that makes you feel even more thirsty and dry inside. That’s called getting **dehydrated**.

But when you get a **saline IV at the doctor’s**, it’s a little different! The doctors and nurses are very careful. They mix just the right amount of salt and water, kind of like making special plant food for your body. Your body needs a little bit of salt to work right, but not too much. The IV gives you the perfect mix so your body can use it and keep you hydrated.

They **don’t use just regular water** in the IV because your body needs some salt to help your blood and cells work properly. If you only got plain water, your body might get too little salt, and that’s not good either. So, they use the just-right mix to help you feel better!

So, it’s all about the **right amount of salt** and giving it in the **right way**—inside your vein when you’re sick, not in your tummy when you drink from the ocean!
